title: Module cohomology is abelian cohomology
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $T$ be a scheme and write
$\mathrm{For}:\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Ab(T_{\Et})$ for the functor forgetting
the $\Lambda$-module structure.

1. If $I$ is an injective object of $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, then for every
   étale $U\to T$ one has $H^q(U_{\Et},\mathrm{For}\,I)=0$ for $q>0$.
2. For every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules and every étale $U\to T$, the
   derived functors of $\Gamma(U,-)$ computed in $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and
   in $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ agree: $\mathrm{For}\,H^q_{\Lambda}(U,F)\cong
   H^q(U,\mathrm{For}\,F)$ canonically.
3. For a morphism $u:S\to T$ and $F\in\Mod(S_{\Et},\Lambda)$ there are
   canonical isomorphisms $\mathrm{For}\,R^qu_*F\cong R^qu_*\mathrm{For}\,F$,
   and for $K\in D^+(S_{\Et},\Lambda)$ a canonical isomorphism
   $\mathrm{For}\,Ru_*K\cong Ru_*\mathrm{For}\,K$ in $D^+(T_{\Et},\mathbf Z)$.

The forgetful functor need not preserve injectives; only the acyclicity of
(1) is used.

proof.text: Fix a universe large enough to contain the chosen small étale sites, coefficient values, morphisms and covering indices. Put $\mathcal O=\underline\Lambda_T$. The étale module-sheaf enough-injectives theorem supplies enough injectives for $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $\Ab(T_{\Et})$. The exact-forgetting theorem applies on this site and says that $\mathrm{For}$ preserves kernels and cokernels. Consequently it preserves images and cohomology: applying it to $\ker d^q/\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$ gives $\ker(\mathrm{For}\,d^q)/\operatorname{im}(\mathrm{For}\,d^{q-1})$. In particular it sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and acts termwise on $D^+$, preserving the bound.

source.place: Tag 03FD, proof, exact forgetting and enough injectives; underlying inputs: sites-modules.tex Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian), injectives.tex Tag 01DU (theorem-sheaves-modules-injectives)

proof.text: We use the same object-cohomology convention in all clauses. For an étale $U\to T$, the localization theorem identifies derived evaluation $R^q\Gamma(U,-)(G)$ on $T_{\Et}$ with the cohomology of $G|_U$ on $T_{\Et}/U$. The étale-site localization equivalence identifies this last site with $U_{\Et}$, carrying $(V\to U)\mapsto G(V)$ and terminal evaluation to restriction and global sections on $U_{\Et}$. Thus this object-cohomology is precisely $H^q(U_{\Et},G|_U)$, the notation in clause (1).

Apply the ringed-site module/abelian evaluation comparison with $\mathcal C=T_{\Et}$, $\mathcal O=\underline\Lambda_T$, $M=I$ and the arbitrary object $U$. Its small-site, common-universe and enough-injectives hypotheses were supplied in step 1. It identifies $H^q(U,\mathrm{For}\,I)$ with $R^qE_U(I)$, where $E_U(P)=P(U)$ is regarded as an abelian group. This is an additive left exact functor: addition and kernels are computed sectionwise. If $I$ is injective, the injective-vanishing theorem gives $R^qE_U(I)=0$ for $q>0$. Combining this with step 2 proves clause (1), without asserting injectivity of $\mathrm{For}\,I$.

For an arbitrary $F$, apply that same ringed-site comparison to obtain $R^qE_U(F)\cong H^q(U,\mathrm{For}\,F)$, naturally in $F$, with identity on sections in degree zero. This is the left side of clause (2) after forgetting coefficients: on a module injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ both $R^qE_U(F)$ and $\mathrm{For}\,H^q_\Lambda(U,F)$ are $\ker(d^q:I^q(U)\to I^{q+1}(U))/\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$ as abelian groups. Forgetting ordinary module coefficients preserves this kernel and quotient by their elementwise definitions. This canonical identification composed with the cited canonical comparison proves clause (2) in every nonnegative degree.

source.place: Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), objectwise equality and its universal-delta-functor normalization

proof.text: Apply the existing canonical derived direct-image comparison to $u:S\to T$ in the category of sheaves valued in $\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda)$. Relate this to the category of sheaves of modules over $\underline\Lambda$ using the explicit constant-ring equivalence: its inverse $C_X$ restricts scalars along the constant-ring presheaf sheafification map and retains the underlying abelian presheaf. The direct-image definition gives $C_T(u_*M)(V)=M(S\times_TV)=(u_*C_SM)(V)$. For $\lambda\in\Lambda$, the scalar on the first term acts through $\Lambda\to\underline\Lambda_T(V)\to\underline\Lambda_S(S\times_TV)$; the composite is the constant-scalar map used on the second term, by the defining property of the ring map $\rho:\underline\Lambda_T\to u_*\underline\Lambda_S$. Restriction maps and maps of sheaves are the same on both sides. This proves the natural direct-image square and identifies its underlying-abelian evaluation identity. Each $C_X$ is an additive equivalence, hence exact by preservation of kernels and cokernels, and preserves injectives: a monomorphism and a lifting problem are carried by the inverse exact equivalence to a monomorphism and a lifting problem in the original category. Termwise, $C_X$ therefore identifies injective resolutions and their direct-image complexes. Consequently the cited fixed derived comparison, obtained by deriving that evaluation identity, gives the canonical natural isomorphism $\mathrm{For}\,Ru_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*\mathrm{For}\,K$ for every $K\in D^+(S_{\Et},\Lambda)$. The sizes are those of step 1; the comparison has no properness, torsion or flatness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0D6J (lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded), part (3), restricted to D+; Tag 03FD and Tag 072W (lemma-higher-direct-images); sites-modules.tex Section 093I (section-constant) for the explicit constant-scalar encoding

proof.text: Take $K=F[0]$ in step 5 and apply degree-$q$ cohomology. By the kernel/image calculation of step 1, the left cohomology sheaf is $\mathrm{For}\,\mathcal H^q(Ru_*F[0])=\mathrm{For}\,R^qu_*F$. The right cohomology sheaf is $\mathcal H^q(Ru_*(\mathrm{For}\,F)[0])=R^qu_*\mathrm{For}\,F$. These are the definitions of higher direct images, and $\mathrm{For}(F[0])=(\mathrm{For}\,F)[0]$ termwise. Thus the fixed comparison gives the sheaf isomorphisms in clause (3), including degree zero. All claims have used exactness and acyclicity, with no claim that forgetting preserves injectives.

proof_origin.place: The three numbered clauses and the companion .proof.md; existing general ringed-site tools supply the same module/abelian comparisons (Stacks Tags 03FD and 0D6J(3)).
